analysts.summary: 21 Buy, 3 Strong Buy, 3 Hold, 0 Sell (MarketBeat). Recent actions: Rosenblatt initiated Buy at $2,400 (9/22), JPMorgan initiated Overweight at $2,250 (8/14), Wedbush Outperform at $2,000, Mizuho trimmed to $1,875 (8/25), UBS Overweight at $1,750, and Zacks cut to Hold (9/7). Consensus EPS is ~$209 for FY27 and ~$252 for FY28.

bear: Peak-cycle margins (84.6% GM) in a commodity industry that has historically reversed sharply.
Slowest QoQ growth among the top five NAND vendors in 2Q26, and it's the smallest by share.
CEO sold ~$105M in September; no insider buying.
Beta ~5 and 75% realised vol: 25% drawdowns (June to August) are routine.
Competitors (Micron, SK hynix) are adding NAND supply; any capex shift from DRAM/HBM to NAND would pressure pricing.
bull: Guided Q1 FY27 revenue $10.3–10.8B and EPS $44–46, above consensus, with GM of 83–85%.
Over 1/3 of FY27 output is pre-sold on multi-year contracts with price floors, which smooths the cycle.
Net cash, $11.5B FCF and $15.5B of buyback capacity (~6% of market cap).
~8x forward P/E is cheap if AI-storage demand keeps NAND tight into 2027–28.
IV near 52-week lows makes hedged or long-premium exposure inexpensive.

competition.summary: Sandisk is the #5 NAND vendor by revenue. In 2Q26 its revenue grew 50.7% QoQ, the slowest of the top five, as it kept bit-shipment growth conservative while Micron (+99%) took third place. It competes with Samsung, SK hynix/Solidigm, Micron and its own JV partner Kioxia. Its edge is BiCS8 density and a high datacenter mix. AI enterprise-SSD demand plus suppliers prioritising DRAM/HBM capex keep NAND tight into 3Q26 (TrendForce).

insiders.summary: Selling only, with no open-market buys. CEO David Goeckeler sold ~67.7K shares (~$105M) on Sep 14 and Sep 17 under a 10b5-1 plan and still holds 382,865 shares. Smaller planned sales came from a director and the legal chief. Insider ownership is ~0.44%.

options.strategy: With IV near 52-week lows ahead of Micron (9/30) and Sandisk earnings in November, buying premium is better value than selling it. Holders could collar (sell ~$2,000 call, buy ~$1,500 put) to protect gains cheaply. Directional bulls could use a Nov $1,800/$2,100 call spread. Informational only; no orders placed.

summary: Sandisk is a pure-play NAND supplier riding an AI-driven flash shortage: FY26 revenue rose 175% to $20.2B, Q4 gross margin hit 84.6% and Q1 FY27 guidance ($10.3–10.8B revenue, $44–46 EPS) points higher still. At $1,772 the stock trades ~8.3x forward earnings, in line with Micron (~7.4x), and our peer-multiple, cycle-adjusted DCF and analyst-target checks converge on a ~$1,500–2,075 fair range with a ~$1,790 midpoint, so it looks fairly valued. The debate is duration of peak margins, not current earnings; multi-year contracts help, but memory is historically boom-bust and the CEO is selling steadily under a 10b5-1 plan. Neutral, low conviction: the range is wide and highly sensitive to NAND pricing.

valuation.method: (a) Peer multiples: 7–9x forward P/E (memory peer MU at 7.4x) on consensus FY27 EPS ~$209 → $1,463–1,881 (mid $1,672). HDD peers WDC/STX trade at 23–26x but have less cyclical pricing, so they were not used for the core range. (b) Cycle-adjusted DCF: FCF $28B FY27, $32B FY28, $24B FY29 (normalisation), terminal FCF $18B growing 2%, 10% discount rate, +$4.6B net cash, 147M shares → ~$1,680. (c) Analyst targets: avg ~$2,016 (range $322–3,050). Triangulated mid = average of the three centres ≈ $1,790; range $1,500–2,075.
valuation.note: Peer revenue growth wasn't available on the pages read. The forward P/E is on peak-cycle consensus EPS. If NAND pricing holds into FY28 (management targets mid/high-teens growth and ~80% GM for FY28–30), fair value moves toward $2,300+. A pricing reversal like 2023 would cut it well below $1,500.
